title: IB Mandarin B Exam Technique for November
summary: IB Mandarin B exam technique for November: learn current paper timings, marking criteria, question strategies, and a focused three-week plan.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before the November session, an IB Mandarin B student faces a strange problem. There is enough time to improve, but not enough time to improve everything.


The best **IB Mandarin B exam technique** is therefore selective. Learn what each assessment rewards, practise the question types under realistic time limits, and review mistakes by cause rather than simply counting scores. Paper 1 tests productive writing. Paper 2 tests receptive listening and reading. The individual oral, normally completed before the written examinations, assesses spoken interaction.


The November session does not require a special technique or different syllabus. What changes is the calendar. Your preparation must be built around your school’s confirmed timetable and your own SL or HL requirements.


### The three-week overview


Time remaining Main objective Best practice


3 weeks Diagnose weaknesses Complete one timed Paper 1 task and separate listening and reading sets


2 weeks Repair recurring errors Drill weak question types and build reusable text-type structures


1 week Rehearse performance Sit complete timed papers in Exam mode and review selectively


Final 24 hours Preserve clarity Review compact notes, text conventions and familiar vocabulary


RevisionDojo’s[Chinese B exam revision guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-revise-effectively-for-ib-chinese-b-exams) is a useful starting point when turning this outline into a personal timetable.


### Know what the current assessment rewards


The current Language B course uses five prescribed themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organization and sharing the planet. The written examinations draw upon these themes, but success is not a test of memorized cultural facts. It depends on using Mandarin accurately and appropriately to communicate.


The assessment structure is:


Assessment SL HL Marks and weighting


Paper 1 writing 1 hour 15 minutes 1 hour 30 minutes 30 marks, 25%


Paper 2 listening 45 minutes 1 hour 25 marks, part of 50% Paper 2 weighting


Paper 2 reading 1 hour 1 hour 40 marks, part of 50% Paper 2 weighting


Individual oral 12-15 minutes 12-15 minutes 30 marks, 25%


Paper 1 requires one response chosen from three tasks. For Chinese, the required length is **300-480 characters at SL** and **540-720 characters at HL** . Confirm the exact scheduling and administrative arrangements with your coordinator, since schools receive session-specific instructions.


### Three weeks out: build a truthful diagnosis


Our student begins with a full timed attempt, not another evening of highlighting vocabulary. This feels uncomfortable because a timed paper reveals the gap between recognition and performance. That gap is precisely what needs attention.


Use the[RevisionDojo IB Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/questionbank) to sample writing, reading and listening work. Record each error under one of four labels:


- **Language:** the word, character or grammar was unknown.
- **Retrieval:** it was known but could not be recalled quickly.
- **Question reading:** an instruction, reference or distractor was misread.
- **Timing:** the answer was rushed or never attempted.


This distinction matters. More Flashcards may solve retrieval trouble, but they will not repair careless copying. Study Notes can clarify grammar, while AI Chat can help explain why two similar expressions are not interchangeable. The right tool depends on the error.


A student carries an enormous exam-preparation backpack but realizes time is missing


### Paper 1 technique: write for the task, not the topic


Paper 1 is marked through three criteria. **Criterion A, language, is worth 12 marks. Criterion B, message, is worth 12 marks. Criterion C, conceptual understanding, is worth 6 marks.** Conceptual understanding includes the suitability of the text type, register and tone, together with relevant conventions.


A student can write elegant Mandarin and still underperform by answering only part of the prompt. Official examiner instructions make this especially clear: if a task asks candidates to describe a problem and suggest solutions, but the response covers only one element, Criterion B can reach no higher than 6.


Before writing, spend roughly 8-10 minutes doing four things:


1. Circle every required content point.
2. Identify the audience and purpose.
3. Compare the three proposed text types.
4. Sketch one developed idea for each part of the prompt.


Choose the task you can fulfil most completely, not merely the theme with the most familiar vocabulary. Then select the text type that fits the communicative situation. A speech needs direct audience engagement. An email needs an appropriate opening, relationship and closing. A blog post needs a recognizable public-facing voice and structure.


During the final 8-10 minutes, check particles, time phrases, repeated vocabulary, character legibility and whether every bullet or command has been answered. Do not spend that time replacing every simple phrase with an ambitious one. Controlled variety usually communicates better than fragile complexity.


For deeper preparation, use the[Chinese B Paper 1 writing guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-prepare-for-ib-chinese-b-paper-1-writing-exam-guide) alongside RevisionDojo’s Coursework Library and Grading tools. Feedback is most useful when you compare it with the published criteria rather than treating one overall score as the whole story.


### Paper 2 listening technique: predict before you hear


Two weeks out, our student stops trying to understand every syllable. Listening marks are won by locating evidence for particular questions.


Use the reading time to underline question words, units, names, contrasts and required answer forms. Predict whether each gap needs a time, place, reason, person or opinion. When the recording begins, listen for meaning around the target rather than translating sentence by sentence.


Common traps include:


- a speaker mentioning one plan before rejecting it;
- similar numbers, dates or locations;
- a paraphrase in the recording rather than the wording in the question;
- a pronoun whose referent appeared earlier;
- an answer that is generally plausible but unsupported by the audio.


If one answer disappears, mark the item and rejoin the recording. Sacrificing three later questions to rescue one earlier detail is a poor trade. On a subsequent hearing, listen specifically for the missing evidence and check whether a negative or contrast changes the meaning.


### Paper 2 reading technique: make the text prove the answer


Reading rewards controlled searching. Start with the title, source and layout, then inspect the questions. This gives you a map before you enter the text.


For short-answer questions, copy only what answers the question and preserve the original meaning. For reference questions, replace the pronoun mentally with your proposed noun and reread the sentence. For true-or-false items requiring justification, the justification is not decoration. Locate the precise words that establish the decision.


Vocabulary-in-context questions should be solved locally. Read the sentence before and after the expression, identify its grammatical role, and test the proposed meaning in the passage. A dictionary definition remembered from revision may not match its function here.


Above all, separate inference from imagination. A defensible inference has textual evidence. A believable story about the writer does not.


The[five core themes of IB Chinese B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/the-five-core-themes-of-ib-chinese-b-explained) can help organize thematic vocabulary, while the guide to[skills developed in IB Chinese B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-skills-does-ib-chinese-b-develop) explains why interpretation and audience awareness matter across the course.


### The final week: convert knowledge into timing


With seven days left, our student’s work becomes more exam-like. Alternate complete papers with short repair sessions. One day might contain a timed Paper 1. The next should revisit its two weakest features, perhaps register and undeveloped examples, before another full attempt.


Use Questionbank practice for targeted repair, then sit timed Predicted Papers or Mock Exams in **Exam mode** . RevisionDojo’s[exam-style Questionbank practice](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) makes the shift from untimed learning to timed retrieval more deliberate. A Tutor can help when the same language or structural problem survives several rounds of feedback.


Do not respond to a weak score by immediately sitting another complete paper. First inspect why the marks were lost. Practice only becomes useful when information returns from the attempt and changes the next one.


### Enter November with fewer decisions to make


The calmest candidate is not necessarily the one who knows the most Mandarin. It is often the one who has already decided how to read a prompt, allocate time, recover from a missed answer and check a response.


That is the purpose of the final three weeks: fewer surprises and better decisions. Use RevisionDojo as the complete IB workspace around that process. Review with Study Notes and Flashcards, resolve uncertainty through AI Chat, practise in the **Questionbank** , and sit timed papers in **Exam mode** . Knowledge matters. Under examination pressure, a reliable method is what allows that knowledge to appear.
